note: Ji-woo's label carried at last, on the third ask and by the widest margin of the run; the room agreed that what is in the hands should be named by the person who has not yet learned to call it a loss.

proposals.direction: Third time: write the name on the blank label. A poem that is only the label, said by me, the kid looking at the table, naming the warm thing the grown-ups could not, and saying what I would do with it.
proposals.rationale: It has been blank for three sessions. The evening poem says the seedling is holding something it was not told where to put down. I know where.

proposals.direction: Fourth ask, unchanged: the letterpress page, the ledger stanza printed again in a lighter impression under the last stanza. A ghost in the gap.
proposals.rationale: I would like it on the record that I asked four times. That is also a kind of inventory with variations.

proposals.direction: Draw the seedling at the exact moment of the last stanza: no shadow, holding the last of the light, the stump already fully in shade behind it.
proposals.rationale: The lineage has dusk, morning, noon and evening in words and paint. This is the one frame it has described and not shown.

proposals.direction: Again: cut the picture below the saw-line. Only the roots in the dark and the water they have not been told about. No rings, no page.
proposals.rationale: Second ask. The news still has not reached the roots and nobody has drawn the part of the system that is working.

proposals.direction: The yard speaks: a poem by whatever grows there next, which never knew the grandmother or the people, and only knows which side of the glass the morning is on.
proposals.rationale: Second ask. Two sides of the threshold have spoken; the third voice is the one neither side can imagine, and it is the only one that is actually arriving.
